reasoning:
The claim that mRNA COVID-19 vaccines alter or permanently change human DNA is scientifically false. According to consensus from major global health authorities (including the CDC, WHO, and NIH) and peer-reviewed molecular biology literature, mRNA vaccines cannot modify human DNA. 

Mechanistically, the mRNA delivered by the vaccine does not enter the cell's nucleus, which is where human DNA is housed. Instead, it remains in the cytoplasm, where cellular machinery uses it to produce the spike protein before the mRNA is rapidly degraded. Furthermore, human cells do not possess the necessary enzymes (such as reverse transcriptase and integrase) to convert foreign mRNA into DNA and integrate it into the host genome. 

While some fringe sources point to highly criticized in vitro studies (such as a 2022 study by Aldén et al. using Huh7 liver cancer cells) to claim that reverse transcription can occur, these laboratory conditions do not replicate human physiology, and the study did not demonstrate integration into the host genome or permanent alteration of human DNA.
title: mRNA vaccines alter human DNA
